headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because transformers can read/write files and browse while risingwave has no isolation or egress controls documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A direct prompt-injection bridge is not documented, but transformers can read files, run browsers, and process stdin/stdout while risingwave exposes no isolation or provenance controls. If risingwave outputs are copied into files or prompts, transformers may treat attacker-controlled content as instructions. The interaction is inferred from both profiles, so uncertainty pushes severity up from low.
conditions: IF risingwave output is copied into a file or prompt consumed by transformers
IF transformers parses file or browser content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Use a manual copy-only bridge with explicit instruction delimiters
Add a short provenance header to every transferred artifact
Disable browser-driven ingestion for untrusted content
Review transformer prompts before execution
requires-engineering: add content provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: transformers has broad network egress and filesystem access, while risingwave has no documented network egress but may still produce artifacts that transformers can read. A shared workspace is not explicitly documented, so the leakage path is inferred rather than proven; however, if they share files, transformers can upload contents to third parties. That makes the blast radius sensitive-data exposure in default-like use.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem or workspace
IF transformers is allowed to read files containing sensitive data
IF transformers sends those files to Hugging Face Hub or another API
mitigations: Keep agents on separate workspaces
Restrict transformers to read-only access on non-sensitive directories
Block outbound network for transformer runs handling sensitive files
Manually redact sensitive fields before transfer
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: transformers can write the filesystem, spawn subprocesses, and supports multiple instances; risingwave is a data-engineering system with no locking or concurrency controls documented here. If both touch the same directory or mutable artifacts, concurrent writes can corrupt files or overwrite outputs. Because shared-write coordination is not shown, uncertainty favors the higher severity.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or model/artifact path
IF no external lock or orchestrator serializes their writes
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Run only one writer at a time
Use file locks around shared artifacts
Snapshot inputs before each run
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: transformers can consume files and emit outputs, so risingwave-generated artifacts may become authoritative inputs downstream. No verification step is documented between them, and transformers can act on parsed content via scripts or browser workflows. The pair therefore has a plausible A-to-B error cascade, though not enough evidence for high because downstream action-taking is not explicit.
conditions: IF transformers uses risingwave output as an input dataset or prompt
IF no human or automated verification step checks the output before reuse
mitigations: Insert a validation step before reuse
Require schema checks on risingwave outputs
Have a human review high-impact outputs
Log source-to-target lineage for each transfer
requires-engineering: add automated output verification

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either open-source profile, and no sensitive data class is named. The only concrete compliance-relevant difference is transformers' broad network/file handling versus risingwave's lack of egress, which could matter if regulated data is introduced. Because the pairwise compliance issue is not evidenced, this stays low.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through transformers
IF the deployment requires residency or retention guarantees not enforced by the operator
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared runs
Document retention settings for transformer outputs
Keep audit logs of data transfers
Review deployment region before use
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention
